subject: MSA & Order Form — liability ceiling: annual reset vs contract total
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Liability ceiling — initial position and asks

Jordan,

Thanks for the call this morning. To move the MSA/Order Form forward internally I wanted to put Acme's position in writing so your legal team has clarity. High level: Acme is comfortable with a monetary cap but we need (a) a clear approach to sizing the cap tied to fees and (b) a path for annual resets. Our starting asks: 

- Cap = greater of (i) 3x fees paid in the preceding 12 months OR (ii) $2,000,000 (we can discuss the floor).
- Annual reset: cap should be measured on a rolling 12-month billing basis so Acme can reason about exposure year-by-year.
- Carve-outs: security incidents and gross negligence remain subject to higher recovery (we can discuss specific language).
- Consequential damages: Acme asks for broader carve-out; we understand Redwood will want to preserve some exclusions.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept an annualized approach (rolling 12 months) versus a contract-total cap? If not, please propose compromise language and we can loop in procurement/legal to redline.

Appreciate it — I'll be the point at Acme on legal side (procurement CC'd).

— Liam
Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Liability ceiling — initial position and asks

Liam — thanks for the clear note and for laying out Acme's objectives. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (commercial) to weigh in on tolerances and potential tradeoffs. Quick thoughts from a product/commercial lens: 

- We understand the desire for predictability; an annual rolling window aligns to how you consume the service. Our counter concern is open-ended cumulative liability over a multi-year term can create outsized exposure for Redwood.
- Two practical options we think are workable: 
  1) Annualized cap (rolling 12 months): cap = greater of (i) 2x fees in the prior 12 months or (ii) $1,500,000.
  2) Contract-total cap: cap = greater of (i) 3x fees paid during the term or (ii) $5,000,000.

Option 1 preserves Acme's yearly budgeting expectations; option 2 gives Redwood predictability on aggregate exposure. Both include the standard carve-outs we anticipate (IP indemnity, gross negligence, breaches of confidentiality, willful misconduct). We expect to exclude consequential damages (mutual carve-out) but allow direct damages and certain statutory remedies.

Laura / Karthik — can you flag any absolute deal-breakers (insurance offsets, consequential carveout scope, survival period) so I can present a single compromise to Acme?

Next step: if Acme prefers option 1, we'll produce a redline of the MSA + order form showing annualized language and proposed monetary floors. If option 2, we'll show contract-total math.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Liability ceiling — initial position and asks

Jordan / Karthik — read Liam's note and Jordan's framing. Below are legal's redline-level concerns and a suggested compromise clause set. Quoted Liam's ask for context: 

> "Cap = greater of (i) 3x fees paid in the preceding 12 months OR (ii) $2,000,000"
> "Annual reset: cap should be measured on a rolling 12-month billing basis"

Legal considerations: 
- Annual reset is acceptable but only if accompanied by a term cap floor (to avoid repeated small payments creating unlimited cumulative exposure). Reasonable compromise: annual cap = 2x prior 12 months fees, with a per-year floor of $1,000,000 and a contract-aggregate cap that is no less than 150% of total fees paid during the term. This gives both sides a ceiling and prevents repeated multi-year exposure stacking beyond a negotiated ratio.
- Consequential damages: Redwood should keep a mutual consequential damages exclusion but permit carve-ins for (i) bodily injury, (ii) payment obligations, and (iii) direct IP claims where remedies exceed insurance. Avoid broad carve-ins tied to lost business unless narrowly defined.
- Security incident carve-out: we will accept a security carve-out allowing for direct incident-related costs but propose a capped remedy tied to 12 months of fees or actual remediation costs, whichever is lower. Also require exhaustion of insurance and coordination with incident response.
- Insurance offsets & indemnity: do not accept a provision that allows offsets against the liability cap for insurance proceeds in all cases; allow set-off only to the extent of actual insurance recoveries and only after gross negligence or willful misconduct findings.

Suggested sample language (to include in redline): 
"The liability of each party for damages arising under this Agreement shall be limited to the greater of (a) two times (2x) the fees paid by Customer to Provider in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, subject to a per-contract aggregate floor equal to one and one-half times (1.5x) total fees paid during the term, and (b) US $1,000,000. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section shall not limit liability for (i) death or personal injury resulting from a party's negligence, (ii) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (iii) a party's indemnification obligations, or (iv) amounts payable for infringement of intellectual property rights."

We will draft a redlined MSA and a short Order Form spreadsheet showing the math for both options and the preferred legal text. If Acme insists on 3x annually as a floor, we can push to increase the contract-aggregate cap accordingly.

Attachments to follow: redlined MSA + order form with calculation scenarios.

— Laura
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Liability ceiling — initial position and asks

Liam — appreciate the quick responses today. Attached are two files: (1) ACME_Redlined_MSA_20280731.docx (highlights show the baked-in legal compromise Laura described), and (2) OrderForm_Proposal_20280731.xlsx (two tabs: "Annualized 2x / $1M floor" and "Contract-total 3x / $5M floor" with sample math based on your estimated run-rate). Key callouts in the redline: 

- We propose to move forward with the Annualized option as a default (cap = greater of 2x prior 12 months fees or $1,000,000) but include a contract-aggregate floor equal to 1.5x total fees paid during the term. This is intended to balance Acme's desire for year-by-year predictability and Redwood's need to limit cumulative exposure.
- Security carve-out language narrowed: incident remediation recoveries are capped at the lower of 12 months fees or actual remediation costs; parties must coordinate on remediation and insurance claims.
- Consequential damages remain mutually excluded with narrowly defined carve-ins (payment obligations, bodily injury, IP injunctive remedies).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Acme legal to redline the attached MSA and indicate whether the annualized formula is acceptable. If you prefer the contract-total approach, call that out and we'll update the order form math.
2) Procurement to confirm DocuSign workflow and any procurement PO/terms required.

If helpful, Laura is available for a 30-minute call this week to talk through specific redline language. We can also produce a short 1-pager that shows exposure scenarios by spend level (to make the tradeoffs easier for your CFO/risk team).

Thanks — Jordan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
